name: 112 會考模擬二模（文揚 1～4 冊）英語閱讀
source: 文揚 112 學年九年級第二次國中教育會考模擬測驗（範圍 1～4 冊），答案與解析取自官方題目解說
passages:
Mr. Green teaches at a junior high school. He shared some important facts about World Water Day and clean water in his class on March 22.
Mr. Green: Good morning, students. Today is World Water Day. The first World Water Day was in 1993. This holiday is a day to celebrate water and to think about water problems around the world.
Mr. Green: Now work in groups of six and talk about this question: Why is water important?
Mr. Green: Good! Let’s see. Hmm, you have good points, students.
(Picture on the screen: Water is important — for drinking / for cleaning / for growing plants / for cooking / for making energy / for staying healthy)
Mr. Green: We all need water. We’re lucky to have clean water when we want it. However, about 785 million people in the world do not have clean water to drink. Life is 【arduous】 for them. They often get sick because of drinking dirty water, and many of them even die. In some countries, many children have to walk hours every day to get water for their family. Because of this, they can’t go to school like all of you.
Mr. Green: So, World Water Day is also a day to think about poor people in other countries. What can we do to help more people to get clean water? Let’s talk about it in our next class.
（energy 能源）

Dear Dr. Smith,
I’m Samantha from the US. I’m eight years old. Like you, I love bugs very much. In my free time, I go out to find them in nature. The world of insects interests me, and I can study them for hours.
However, in my new school, the kids do not share my interest. They said things like, “Girls should not like bugs,” “Bug hunting is not right,” “What a strange girl! No one likes her.”
They don’t like the fact that I am different. I once brought a bug from home. One of the kids saw it and killed the poor thing. It really broke my heart.
Now, things are getting worse. More and more kids 【bully】 me. They call me names, laugh at me, or even push me. No one wants to make friends with me. I am lonely at school.
【I’m thinking of giving up my love for bugs】. Will the kids treat me better if I do so?
Samantha

Dear Samantha,
Can I call you a “bug girl”?
Listen, Bug Girl. You are different, and you are special. There is nothing wrong with your love for bugs. Keep up your interest in them.
Remember, everyone has the right to follow their heart.
Bug Lover
Dr. Smith
（bug 小蟲子　right 權利）

Linda and her husband, Eric, run a donkey ride business. They had a special experience with Herbert, a baby donkey, last year.
Linda wrote down this experience in her diary.
June 12: It is sad that three-month-old Herbert’s mother does not like him. She does not want to feed him or get close to him. The baby’s health is getting worse. Eric and I must do something to help the poor thing, or he will die soon.
June 13: Last night, we took Herbert into the house. He looked so weak. He couldn’t even stand on his feet. All night, I sat by his side and fed him milk from bottles every hour.
June 14: Eric bought big dog nappies from the pet store. Little Herbert looked really cute in a nappy.
June 21: Herbert is getting better. He enjoys being with our pet dogs in the garden during the day.
July 5: Something interesting happened during the past week. Herbert started to play with a ball, go for a walk with me, and run with the dogs. In many ways, he acts just like his dog friends.
July 22: Herbert is growing well. He has all his teeth. Best of all, he is eating well. It means that it is time for him to join the other donkeys on the farm.
July 25: Herbert is not around the house. He began to live with the other donkeys in a paddock yesterday. My cute boy will do fine.
（donkey 驢子　diary 日記　weak 虛弱的　nappy 尿布　paddock 圍場）

【群組聊天】Sherry, Jim, Vivien, Greg, Brian…(8)
Sherry: （傳了一張照片：一個戴著紅色塑膠鼻子的男子）
Sherry: Hey, guys! Look at the picture above. Isn’t he George Wood, the popular singer? Why is he wearing a plastic red nose? He looks really funny.
Jim: Well, he’s not doing it just for fun. He’s also celebrating Red Nose Day to raise money to help people in need in Africa and in the UK. The money also goes to help build a healthy future for children.
Vivien: Wow! He has a great heart.
Jim: 👍
Jim: You know, for many families around the world, putting food on the table is a struggle. So, their children always go hungry and are in poor health. Many famous people like George Wood are doing their part to help keep these children safe and healthy.
Greg: Is it possible for us to join Red Nose Day, too?
Jim: It’s as easy as pie. We can order a box of red noses or more on the Internet. The money will be life-changing for some children in the world.
Brian: But…
Sherry: But what?
Brian: Wearing a red nose in public?
Sherry: Come on. It’ll make a change in other people’s life. Let’s do it and have fun.
Jim: I’ll join in.
Greg: Count me in.
Vivien: 🆗
Brian: No, thank you. I’ll just give some money to poor families in town.
（plastic 塑膠的　raise 募款　struggle 掙扎）

Kevin, a junior high school student, loves potatoes. He is planning to visit Idaho Potato Museum during summer vacation. Last night, he found some interesting facts about potatoes and the museum on the Internet. The following are his notes.
【potatoes】
1. There are more than 4,000 kinds in the world.
2. They come in different shapes and sizes.
3. A potato is about 80% water and 20% solids.
4. It is better to store them in a dry, dark place.
5. They are a kind of vegetable and are good for health.
6. Wash them only before cooking them.
【Idaho Potato Museum】
• opened in 1988
• shows the history of potatoes in Idaho and many interesting things about this plant
• has a gift shop and a coffee shop
【Where】130 NW Main Street, Blackfoot, ID 83221, USA
【Opening hours】
September～May: 9:30a.m.～5:00p.m. Mon-Sat
June～August: 9:30a.m.～7:00p.m. Mon-Sat; 9:30a.m.～5:00p.m. Sun
Closed: Thanksgiving, Christmas & New Year’s Day
【Tickets】
Adults: $6　Seniors: $5.50　Children 5-12: $3　Children 4 & Under: Free　Groups of 15 or more: $5 each
（potato 馬鈴薯　solid 固體　store 儲存　adult 成人　senior 老年人）

Jason is interested in electric cars. Last week he made a report about these modern cars.
【What are electric cars?】
Electric cars do not run on gas. They use battery power to heat and cool. It usually takes 300 smartphone batteries to make one battery for an electric car.
【Who made the first electric car in the world?】
Around 1832-1839, Robert Anderson built an early electric car.
【How were the sales of electric cars in the world from 2019 to 2022?】
See picture 1.（長條圖：2019 年約 7,000,000 輛出頭，2020 年約 10,000,000 輛，2021 年約 16,000,000 輛，2022 年約 26,000,000 輛）
【Top 5 countries with the most electric cars for every 1,000 residents in 2020】
In 2020, electric cars already became more common around the world, especially in countries like Sweden, Iceland, Norway, Germany, and the Netherlands. Of the five countries, Norway was far ahead, with the most electric cars for every 1,000 residents. Iceland and Sweden were next. Electric cars were more popular in Iceland than in Sweden. Germany and the Netherlands had the fewest electric cars. There were 10.7 electric cars for every 1,000 residents in the Netherlands and 8.5 in Germany.
【What are the good points and bad points of electric cars?】
Good points: *They are cleaner and quieter than gas-powered cars. *They save money on gas. *Some electric cars can really go very fast.
Bad points: *They can be very expensive. *Charging electric cars is slow. It may take at least 30 minutes to get 80% charged. *The battery may become weak over time.
（electric 電的　battery 電池　resident 居民　especially 特別地　charge 充電）

Isabella Wilson is from the US. She has a great job, and she likes it very much.
Several years ago, Isabella got her first job, and then she began to work 80-100 hours a week. One day, she thought to herself, “What a life! I work, work, and work! I’m really sick of all this. I want more sunshine, more exercise, and more time to myself.” Then and there, she decided to leave her job.
Isabella loved traveling, and she dreamed of visiting many parts of the world. In 2017, after she quit her job, she traveled across the US, but she had to think of ways to cut down on expenses. Then in July, 2018, in a book, she found out an interesting job, house sitting.
At the end of 2018, she began to work as a house sitter. What does she do? She stays at and looks after a house when its owners are away. At the same time, she has to take care of their pets. In this way, she stays in an expensive house for free. She can cook, take a bath, and even use the owner’s car to go around. Best of all, she can make some money from the job.
“It’s cost-saving,” Isabella said. For example, in 2020, she took her first trip to the UK for a month without having to spend at least £200 a night at a hotel.
Now, Isabella enjoys her life very much. She is planning to write a book about her experience as a house sitter.
（travel 旅行　quit 離開；辭職　expense 開銷）

Climbing Mount Everest, the highest mountain in the world, is a big dream for many climbers. In 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first people to get to the top of the mountain. From then on, ＿41＿. Now, over 600 people attempt it every climbing season during a few weeks of the year when the weather is just right.
Because Mount Everest stands at 8,849 m, the air there is very thin and cold. ＿42＿. In fact, not every climber can make it. Sadly, some of them might even lose their lives in their attempt. Every year about 5-10 people die on Mount Everest, and the number is rising each year.
When climbers climb Mount Everest, they must carry a lot of things with them. Bottles of oxygen are one of the most important things to keep them safe. They also have to take tents, food, and many other things. Sadly, many of the climbers do not clean up themselves when going down the mountain, and they leave behind what they no longer need behind them. In a lot of pictures, we can see that ＿43＿.
From now on, for the good of nature every climber to Mount Everest should stop leaving trash there. This way, they can enjoy the trip and help the mountain stay clean at the same time.
（attempt 試圖　oxygen 氧氣　tent 帳篷）

questions.q: In the picture, the girl does not look good. She is ＿＿＿＿.
questions.e: 由圖示推知女孩在咬指甲，選(A)。(B)展示她的指甲；(C)揮舞著雙手；(D)洗手。

questions.q: Jack forgot to bring ＿＿＿＿ when he went camping. Without them, it was hard to eat soup.
questions.e: 方便喝湯的餐具為湯匙，選(B)。(A)叉子；(C)刀子；(D)盤子。

questions.q: Even at 90, Vicky’s grandfather is still very ＿＿＿＿. He is working on a new book to put his life story into words.
questions.e: 90歲的人依然在寫新書，推知他仍然很敏銳，選(B)。(A)滑稽的；(C)勇敢的；(D)困難的。

questions.q: Julie is crying over the ＿＿＿＿ of her pet dog; its life just ended.
questions.e: Julie的狗剛結束了一生，推知牠死了，選(C)。(A)年齡；(B)聲音；(D)快樂。

questions.q: Jenny is a happy girl. The smile on her face always ＿＿＿＿ everyone around her.
questions.e: 一個快樂的人臉上的笑容總能照亮別人，選(B)。(A)放棄；(C)為……說話；(D)躲著……。

questions.q: The sun looks ＿＿＿＿ when it goes down than when it is high in the sky.
questions.e: than（比……）用於比較級，選(C)。

questions.q: Paul told Mary to be true to ＿＿＿＿ and not to try to be someone else.
questions.e: Paul提醒Mary要忠於自己，不要試圖成為別人。空格中的人指的是Mary，和前面的Mary為同一人，因此用反身代名詞來指涉，選(C)。

questions.q: Wait here ＿＿＿＿ your father comes, Tony. He’ll pick you up in ten minutes.
questions.e: 說話者命令Tony就地等他父親來接他。表示「一直做某件事直到某個時間」的連接詞用until（直到……為止），選(B)。

questions.q: Hank Anderson is a(n) ＿＿＿＿ writer. He wrote his first book in 2003. All his five books are very popular. He is going to write his sixth one.
questions.e: Hank Anderson在2003年寫了第一本書，他的書都很受歡迎，推知他是個成功的作家，選(D)。(A)拙劣的；(B)可能的；(C)不快樂的。

questions.q: Karen works as a(n) ＿＿＿＿ in Mr. Brown’s office. She spends most of her time answering phones, planning meetings, and doing many other things. She is very helpful to her boss.
questions.e: 和接電話、規劃會議等有關的辦公室工作是祕書，選(B)。(A)律師；(C)女服務生；(D)工程師。

questions.q: ＿＿＿＿ a new boy student in our class next week. Let’s welcome him and get to know him.
questions.e: 表示「存在有……」，用there be表達。未來式用there will be，選(C)。

questions.q: If William ＿＿＿＿ to the U.S. this year, he’ll have to wait at least two years when he has a longer vacation. He has to think about it carefully.
questions.e: If連接表示假設的子句，使用現在簡單式，意味著此假設為一個可能的現實，選(A)。

questions.q: Elsa is already 20 years old, but her father still doesn’t let her ＿＿＿＿ his car. Sometimes she has to borrow one from a friend.
questions.e: let（讓）為使役動詞，後面要接原形動詞，選(B)。

questions.q: Jack called Helen ＿＿＿＿ her to a magic show this Saturday night, but she can’t go. She has a date that night.
questions.e: 表示Jack打電話給Helen的目的，用不定詞，選(D)。

questions.q: Jim thought the science test would be difficult, but ＿＿＿＿, it was quite easy. He got a 92.
questions.e: Jim原本以為自然科考試很難，實際上，相當簡單，選(D)。(A)傷心地；(B)快速地；(C)可怕地。

questions.q: City Zoo in Happy Town is not as popular as it was before. There were only 500 ＿＿＿＿ last month. If it goes on like this, the zoo will have to close.
questions.e: 動物園因為不如以前受歡迎，未來可能關門，推知是遊客數量少，選(A)。(B)工人；(C)動物；(D)郵差。

questions.q: There are several restaurants near the train station. We should try ＿＿＿＿ one next time. This one isn’t good enough.
questions.e: 火車站附近有幾家餐廳，此次用餐的這家餐廳並不令人滿意，下回換在另外一家用餐，並沒有指定哪一家，因此用(A)another。故選(A)。

questions.q: David met his wife when he ＿＿＿＿ in the UK. A year and a half later, they had their first child, Angel. Now the girl is already five.
questions.e: David過去在英國求學時遇見他的太太，求學為過去某段時間所持續的事件，用過去進行式表達，選(B)。

questions.q: If you want to stay warm outside in winter, ＿＿＿＿ a coat when you leave home. It’ll be even better if you wear a hat and gloves, too.
questions.e: if連接表示條件的子句，從空格到home為命令句，表示「如果……就必須……」的意思，選(A)。

questions.q: When Jean entered her house, she saw a man in the living room, so she shouted at him, “Who are you? Go away right now, or ＿＿＿＿ the police.”
questions.e: Jean命令在她家客廳裡的陌生男子立刻離開，否則(or)她會報警。報警這個動作，在當時並還沒有發生，用未來式表達，選(B)。

questions.q:
Jim: A nice jacket, Terry.
Terry: Thanks. It doesn’t ＿＿＿＿ a thing. It’s a gift from my brother.
questions.e: Terry的夾克是哥哥送的禮物，推知它是免費的。表示物品的價值用cost，選(C)。

questions.q:
Jack: I saw you ＿＿＿＿ for the bus on Park Street around three this afternoon.
Nancy: Yeah, I had a guitar class at four.
questions.e: see為感官動詞。看到某人正在做某件事，後面＋V-ing，選(B)。

questions.q:
Tom didn’t understand the meaning of “heed” in the reading below:
Jerry got to the party an hour late last night because he did not heed the road sign on Park Street. When he was driving on that street, he got a phone call from his boss. Because of this, he missed the sign. He then turned left and drove to the other side of the city.
What does “heed” most likely mean here?
questions.e: Jerry在Park街接到電話，因而錯過標誌，走錯路，推知heed最適當的意思為留意，選(C)。(A)在乎；(B)聽；(D)照料。

questions.q: What does 【arduous】 mean in the reading?
questions.e: 世界上約有7.85億人並沒有乾淨的水可喝，推知arduous的意思為(C)艱難的。(A)無聊的；(B)簡單的；(D)方便的。故選(C)。

questions.q: What is NOT the purpose of Mr. Green’s class on March 22?（purpose 目的）
o: To ask students to share ways of saving water.
To point out water problems in the world.
To teach students to care about poor people.
To have students think about the uses of water.
questions.e: Green先生在3月22日的課堂中並沒有要求學生分享省水的方式，選(A)。(B)指出世界的水問題；(C)教導學生關懷窮人；(D)讓學生思考水的用途。

questions.q: What does it mean when people 【bully】 a person?
o: They are afraid of him or her.
They treat him or her like a friend.
They say something nice to him or her.
They do something to make him or her feel terrible.
questions.e: 罵人、嘲笑人，甚至推人，都是讓人覺得很糟糕的事情，推知bully（霸凌）的意思為(D)。(A)他們害怕他或她；(B)他們把他或她當做朋友；(C)他們對他或她說一些好話。故選(D)。

questions.q: Why does Samantha say, “I’m thinking of giving up my love for bugs”?
o: She is tired of studying bugs.
She is going to learn something else.
She is too busy to spend time with her friends.
She wants other kids to become friends with her.
questions.e: 由下一句得知Samantha考慮放棄自己的愛好，看看這樣做，別的小孩能不能對她好一點，選(D)。(A)她對研究小蟲子感到厭倦了；(B)她將學些別的東西；(C)她太忙了，沒有時間和朋友在一起，都不是她說這句話的原因。

questions.q: What is the reading mainly about?
questions.e: 這篇文章主要是敘述Linda親自照顧驢寶寶Herbert，救了牠一命，選(A)。(B)Herbert和牠的狗朋友、(C)一隻母驢的生命故事、(D)在農場上養驢，都不是文章的重點。

questions.q: According to Linda’s diary, which is WRONG?（according to 根據）
o: Linda took care of Herbert for about 6 weeks.
Herbert spent much of his early life with the family dogs.
Herbert seldom stayed outside when he was under Linda’s care.
questions.e: Herbert白天和狗兒們在花園裡，選(D)。(A)Herbert在Linda悉心照顧下恢復健康；(B)從6月12日到7月24日，約六週；(C)Herbert待在Linda家中時，和狗相處時間多，結果行為就像牠們一樣。

questions.q: How many of Sherry’s friends are going to wear a red nose like George Wood?
questions.e: Sherry線上群組參加討論的四個朋友中只有Brian不願意在公共場合戴紅鼻子，選(C)。

questions.q: According to the dialogue, which is true about Jim?（according to 根據）
o: He is going to give red noses away.
He only cares about famous people.
He knows almost nothing about Red Nose Day.
He wants to make a change in other people’s life.
questions.e: Jim會加入購買紅鼻子，並在公共場合戴，以改變別人的生活，選(D)。(A)他並沒有要捐出紅鼻子；(B)他也關心弱勢；(C)他知道一些有關於紅鼻子日的事實。

questions.q: Which is said about potatoes in Kevin’s notes?
o: Why they are a healthy food.
questions.e: Kevin的筆記提到馬鈴薯大約含有80%的水和20%的固體，選(A)。(B)如何烹煮、(C)它們來自何處、(D)為什麼它們是健康食物，都未提及。

questions.q: Sherry is one of Kevin’s classmates. She visited Idaho Potato Museum during summer vacation in 2022. She wrote something about the trip. Which is most likely true?（likely 可能地）
o: The museum is already very old. It is at least 50 years old…
I enjoyed a nice meal at a restaurant in the museum. All the potato dishes tasted so great…
I visited the museum with my sister Belinda. She is only five, so she did not have to buy a ticket…
Before going home, I bought an Idaho Potato Museum postcard at the gift shop and sent it to myself…
questions.e: Idaho馬鈴薯博物館有禮品店，選(D)。(A)博物館在1988年開業，還不到50年；(B)博物館內並沒有餐廳；(C)5-12歲兒童票價為$3。

questions.q: According to Kevin’s notes, which is NOT true about Idaho Potato Museum?
o: It is open to people of all ages.
It is open on Sundays only in summer.
It is closed during the Chinese New Year.
Most of the year, it is open for seven and a half hours a day.
questions.e: 博物館在新年關閉而非中國春節期間，選(C)。(A)開放給各個年齡層的人、(B)只有在夏季，星期日才有開放、(D)一年大部分的時間，它每天開放七個半小時，都是正確的敘述。

questions.q: What do we know about electric cars from Jason’s report?
o: The owners of electric cars can charge it at home.
They are becoming more and more popular around the world.
questions.e: 由2019年到2022年全球電動車銷售量統計圖可推知電動車越來越受歡迎，選(D)。(A)它們開起來很有趣、(B)它們越來越好、(C)電動車主人可在自家充電，都未提及。

questions.q: Who will find Jason’s report helpful?
o: Stella. She wants to know how an electric car works.
William. He wants to know how fast an electric car runs.
Lucy. She wants to know how far an electric car can go on one charge.
Oliver. He wants to know how many kinds of electric cars there are on the market.
questions.e: 文章中提及電動車不使用汽油行駛，而是使用電池，選(A)。(B)電動車能跑多快、(C)電動車充一次電能跑多遠、(D)市場上有多少種電動車，都未提及。

questions.q: Which is true about the top five countries with the most electric cars for every 1,000 residents in 2020?（選項見圖）
questions.e: 2020年，提到的五個國家中，挪威以每1,000名居民中擁有最多的電動車領先，接著為冰島、瑞典、荷蘭及德國，故選(C)。

questions.q: What is the reading mostly about?
questions.e: 這篇文章主要在談論Isabella為人看屋的新工作，選(A)。(B)Isabella Wilson的忙碌的工作、(C)Isabella Wilson對寵物的愛、(D)Isabella Wilson的旅遊經驗，都不是文章的主要重點。

questions.q: According to the reading, which happened last?
o: Isabella Wilson quit her first job.
Isabella Wilson traveled in the UK.
Isabella Wilson traveled a lot in her own country.
